transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. It’s really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... I came in today because... well, I’ve just been having a hard time shaking this... this really heavy feeling. I mean, I know I should probably be able to just push through it, and I really don't want to sound overly dramatic or anything, but it’s just been feeling a bit hopeless lately. It’s almost like... like everything I worked so hard to build back up after my divorce has just completely collapsed, and I’m just sort of... sitting under it all. 

I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things okay.
Did this heavy, hopeless feeling start after your divorce?

Well, no, not exactly right after the divorce itself. The divorce was hard, of course, but I actually thought I was handling it pretty well for a while. I was really trying to stay positive. 

It was more... um, I guess it started about a month ago. There was just this whole financial mess that came up from the settlement, and... I don't know, it just felt like too much all at once. That's when this cloud kind of settled over me, and it just hasn't lifted for the last four weeks or so. 

I feel terrible complaining about it, because I know people go through much worse financial stuff all the time. Am I making a bigger deal out of this than I should be? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
When you notice this heavy, hopeless feeling, does it seem mostly connected to the financial settlement situation?

Well, um... I guess it started with the financial stuff, but... it's kind of become more than that now. I really hope I'm not sounding like I'm just feeling sorry for myself, but... it's just this constant, heavy feeling that I can't seem to shake. 

It's like... even when I try to focus on other things, or when I'm at work—I'm a civil engineer, so I really need to be able to focus—it's just always there. That hopeless feeling. Like I mentioned before, it really just feels like everything I tried to rebuild is just gone, and I'm just stuck under the weight of it all. 

Does that make sense? I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. I know I should be handling this better.
Before this past month, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for days or weeks at a time?

Um... no, I really don't think so. I mean, I've had normal bad days, you know? Like everyone does. But nothing that lasted for weeks or felt this... heavy. I’ve always been pretty good at just pushing through things and staying productive. 

I hope I'm not forgetting anything important... I really want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information. But as far as I can remember, this is the first time it's ever been like this for me. Is that okay? I'm sorry if that's not very helpful for figuring things out, I just want to be as accurate as I can for you.
Do you feel this sadness is stronger than you would normally expect from the financial settlement problem?

Well... yeah, I think so. I mean, I keep telling myself it's just money, right? People deal with financial stress every day, so I really shouldn't be letting it get to me this badly. I feel a little silly even admitting it, but... yes, it does feel a lot stronger than it probably should. 

Honestly, that's... that's the main reason I came in to see you today. I just can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling, no matter how hard I try to push through it. It really just feels like everything I built after the divorce has collapsed, and I’m just sitting under it. 

I hope it's okay that I made an appointment for this. I know I should be stronger, and I really just want to get back to normal so I'm not wasting your time. Am I making sense?
Has this been making it hard for you to function at work or take care of things day to day?

Well, um... yes, it really has. I hate to admit it because I've always prided myself on being reliable, but... things have gotten a bit messy lately. 

At work, I started... well, I guess I was making some questionable calls on project designs. I actually ended up kind of falling apart in a few meetings, which was so embarrassing. My supervisor actually had to step in and take me off active project decisions for now. I feel terrible about it, I really hope they don't think less of me. I just couldn't focus.

And at home... I just kind of stopped keeping up with everything. Basic routines, cooking, cleaning... it all just felt like too much. It actually got bad enough that I... well, I ended up being sent to the emergency department recently because I just... I didn't feel safe with my own thoughts anymore. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds really intense and I probably should have handled it better before it got to that point. I really want to be doing better than this. Does that answer what you were asking? I hope I'm not oversharing...
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself?

Um... well... I guess... I mean, I wouldn't say I've had a plan or anything like that. I know how terrible that would be for everyone around me, and I really wouldn't want to cause anyone that kind of pain. 

But... I have been having these thoughts lately where I just... I kind of wish I wouldn't wake up. Like it would just be easier if everything stopped. It got a little bit intense the other day, and it actually scared me quite a bit. That's... that's why I ended up calling the employee assistance program at work before I went to the ED. I just wanted to make sure I was doing the right thing and getting help before I did something stupid. 

I feel awful even saying it out loud. I know I shouldn't be thinking that way. I'm really trying to get better, I promise. Is it normal to feel like that when you're this stressed out? I hope you don't think I'm crazy or anything...
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Well... I guess I'd say I'm still trying to keep up with things. I mean, I don't want to just sit around and do nothing, you know? But... I suppose things I usually like doing haven't felt quite as fun lately. 

Like, I usually love going hiking on the weekends, or even just working on little DIY projects around the house. I've tried to force myself to do them because I know I should, but... I just haven't really felt that spark, I guess. I kind of just end up staring at the wall or going back to bed. 

I'm sure it's just because I'm so tired from everything else going on. I really am trying to stay active and positive, I promise. Do you think that's just part of being this stressed out? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is...
Have you been hearing voices or feeling certain of things that other people say aren’t true?

Oh! Um... no. No, definitely not. I mean, I know I've been really overwhelmed lately, and I'm so sorry if I made it sound like things were getting completely out of hand. But I haven't experienced anything like that. No voices or... or believing things that aren't real. 

I'm still very grounded in reality, I promise. I'm just having a hard time managing my stress right now. That's... that's normal for someone going through a rough patch, right? I really hope you don't think I'm completely losing my mind...
Have you noticed a big change in your appetite?

Um... well, my appetite has been pretty normal, I think. I mean, I've been trying really hard to make sure I still eat three meals a day, even when I'm feeling a bit down. I know how important it is to keep my strength up. 

Maybe... maybe I've been eating just a tiny bit less than usual? Just because I've been so tired, you know? Sometimes fixing a whole meal just feels like a lot of work. But I'm definitely not starving myself or anything like that. I've been making sure to at least have some toast or a piece of fruit. 

I'm doing my best to take care of myself, I really am. It's just hard when you're feeling so drained. That's a pretty common reaction to stress, isn't it? Just not feeling super hungry all the time? I hope that doesn't sound too concerning...
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Um... sleep has been... well, I've really been trying to get my eight hours, because I know how important a good routine is. I've been setting a bedtime and trying to wind down, but... I guess I have been having a little bit of trouble lately. 

It's probably just normal stress, right? But sometimes I just... I lie awake staring at the ceiling, and my brain just starts replaying all these little things—like bills I need to pay, or silly mistakes I made at work. I try really hard to push it away. And then, other times, I'll wake up way before dawn, and I just feel like I never actually went to sleep at all. 

I'm sure it's just because I have a lot on my plate right now, and I'm trying to handle it all as best as I can. It's pretty normal to lose a little sleep when you're overwhelmed, isn't it? I just... I hope I'm not doing a bad job of managing everything.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy lately?

Um... well, I wouldn't say "unusually" tired, exactly. I mean, I'm still showing up to work and getting things done. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or just being lazy. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, things have felt a little bit heavier lately. Like, getting through a normal workday kind of feels like... like I'm dragging wet concrete? And sometimes just doing little things, like taking a shower or opening my laptop to start a project, it just takes more energy than I seem to have right now. 

I'm still pushing through it, though! I know everyone gets tired, especially with a demanding job. It's totally normal to feel a bit drained when you're working hard, right? I just hope I'm not letting anyone down by being a little slower than usual...
For the past month, have you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I've given up or anything. I'm really trying to keep a positive attitude. I know I have a lot to be thankful for, and I don't want to sound ungrateful or dramatic. 

But... I guess the reason I finally made the appointment is because... well, I just can't seem to shake this really heavy feeling. It's just... it's been hard to feel hopeful lately. You know, after my divorce, I worked so hard to rebuild my life and get everything back on track. And I did a good job, I really did. But lately, it just kind of feels like... like everything I built has collapsed, and I'm just sort of sitting underneath all the rubble. 

I'm still trying to stay strong, though! I know everyone goes through rough patches, and it's normal to feel a little down sometimes, right? I just... I hope it doesn't make me sound weak for struggling with it this much.
During the past month, have you felt down or hopeless nearly every day?

Um... I'm sorry, I know I sort of just rambled about this a second ago. I hope I'm answering your questions right. But... yes. To be completely honest, it really has been almost every single day this past month. 

Like I was saying, I just... I can't seem to shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It really does feel like everything I tried so hard to build after the divorce has just completely collapsed, and I'm just trapped sitting under it all. 

I really hate admitting that out loud, because it makes me sound so pessimistic, and I promise I'm usually a very capable person at work and everywhere else. I'm really trying my best to push through it. It's okay to admit when things feel a little too heavy, isn't it? I just hope I'm not coming across as too negative...
Do you still have moments when you feel okay, as long as you're not thinking about the financial settlement?

Um... I wish I could say yes, I really do. I know dwelling on things isn't healthy, and I really try hard to just focus on my work and put the settlement completely out of my mind. 

But... honestly, even when I'm completely distracted with a big engineering project or something, that heavy feeling is still just... there. It's like it's constantly running in the background, if that makes sense? I don't want to sound like I'm just wallowing in it, because I promise I'm trying my best to stay positive and keep moving forward. But... no, I haven't really had any moments where I actually feel okay lately, even when I'm not thinking about the divorce stuff. 

I hope I'm explaining that right... I just don't want you to think I'm not trying to help myself feel better.
Over the past month, have you been having trouble concentrating or making decisions?

Um... well, I really try to stay on top of everything at work, I promise. I've always prided myself on being very sharp and reliable. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, I have been struggling a little bit with focus lately. 

It's actually really embarrassing to admit, because I don't want to sound incompetent or anything... but lately, I'll look at a basic drainage calculation, or a spreadsheet I've literally used for years, and my mind just... blanks. I end up just sitting there, rereading the exact same numbers over and over, and I just can't seem to trust myself to make a simple decision on it. 

I always double-check my work, though, so I haven't made any major mistakes! I'm really trying to push through it so I don't let my team down. It's just taking me so much longer to do things I usually do in my sleep. That kind of brain fog can happen when you're under a lot of stress, right? I just hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it...
Over the past month, have you been moving or speaking noticeably slower than usual?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I really try to keep my energy up, especially at the office. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm slacking off or anything. 

I guess I might be a little more tired than usual, just with everything going on, but I definitely haven't been dragging myself around or talking in slow motion or anything like that. I always make sure to keep a smile on my face and respond quickly when people talk to me. I'm still keeping up with everything, I promise. 

I'm probably just my normal self, just... maybe a tiny bit quieter? But definitely not noticeably slower. That's a good thing, right? I'm really trying hard not to let this affect how I interact with people.
Over the past month, have you been feeling worthless or guilty nearly every day?

Um... well, I really try not to think like that. I know it's not productive, and I always try to look on the bright side and focus on being helpful to everyone around me. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it has been a little hard to turn off those negative thoughts lately. I don't want you to think I'm just throwing a pity party or anything, because I really am trying to be strong... but I just keep telling myself that I'm a terrible engineer, and a failed wife, and just... a burden to people. 

It's silly, I know. But I catch myself replaying every little thing, like a missed calculation at work or a tense email, and it just feels like proof that I ruin things. I try so hard to push those thoughts away and just be a good person, but they keep creeping back in. That's probably just a normal reaction to going through a hard time, though, right? I really hope I'm not sounding too dramatic... I just want to be honest so I can get back to being myself.
Over the past month, have you been thinking about death a lot?

Oh... um... I really don't want to sound ungrateful for my life or anything. I know I have a lot to be thankful for, and I would never want to do anything to hurt myself, I promise. 

But... well, I guess if I have to be completely honest... I haven't been thinking about *death* exactly, but... sometimes, lately, I’ve been having these thoughts that it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up. Just so I wouldn't have to keep feeling so heavy or worrying about letting everyone down. 

I feel terrible even saying it out loud to you. But... the thoughts actually did get pretty intense recently. So intense that I kind of scared myself. I didn't want to worry my husband or cause any drama, so I... I actually ended up calling the employee assistance program at work. Just to have someone to talk to so I wouldn't do anything stupid. 

I figured that was the responsible thing to do, right? Reaching out for help before things got worse? I really am trying my best to handle this the right way... I just hope you don't think less of me for having those thoughts in the first place.
